Definition: probably from λείβω (to pour a "libation"); the south(- west) wind (as bringing rain, i.e. (by extension) the south quarter):--southwest.
BiblicalUsage: líps means the south-west wind, and once is enough to see what it is doing. In Acts 27:12, "and lieth toward the south west and north west.".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the south-west wind is the sailor's gamble — a fair wind to Phenice, and a storm waiting beyond it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
